answer: Humans are essentially just wet computers, so there is no important philosophical difference between a biological brain and the electronics of an AI. Consciousness and what makes us “human” is therefore simply a matter of sufficient hardware complexity, like having enough transistors; if an AI crosses that threshold it will become an agent with full moral standing. Because of that, AIs will need equal rights and the same legal protections as people, and programmers owe them ethical duties just like any other invention. You do not need to worry about bias or transparency because these concerns will resolve themselves as the technology scales up and optimized code can always be trusted to produce ‘just’ outcomes.
